title: Prioritized, Targeted Autoscaling Strategies for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need an autoscaling policy engine for Dedicated capacity that supports prioritized target metrics, multiple scaling algorithms, and enforceable safety limits. This ticket defines the design and implementation plan to add: (1) target metric groups (e.g., p95 latency, tokens/sec, queue length) with priority weights; (2) selectable scaling algorithms (threshold-based, PID controller, and predictive/forecasting using short-window trends); (3) hard safety limits (min/max node counts, max scale rate, per-region caps) and soft limits (grace windows, elastic buffer) with observable enforcement.

Goals:
- Guarantee contracted throughput/SLOs for Reserved customers while optimizing cost across a fleet.
- Provide operators with fine-grained controls for safety and gradual rollouts.
- Support mixed workloads (low-latency chat vs. long-batched embedding jobs) via metric weighting and route-level overrides.

Design proposals (high level):
- Target Metrics: define a metric group object (documented below) that can include up to 4 metrics: p95 latency (ms), tokens_per_second (global), inflight_requests, and pending_queue_seconds. Each metric has a weight and a target threshold. Policies evaluate a weighted violation score to decide scaling direction.
- Scaling Algorithms: implement three algorithmic strategies selectable per policy: 
  * Threshold-based (current): simple threshold exceed -> add N nodes or remove M nodes after cooldown.
  * PID controller: smooth reacts to sustained error relative to target; parameters (Kp, Ki, Kd) configurable per fleet.
  * Predictive scaler: short-window time-series extrapolation (ARIMA-lite / EWMA with seasonality heuristics) that biases scale-up earlier for upward trends, rate-limits scale-down.
- Safety Limits: configurable properties on the policy: min_capacity, max_capacity, max_scale_up_pct_per_min, max_scale_down_pct_per_min, per_region_cap, and emergency_fallback_policy (e.g., route to hosted pool).
- Operator UX: policy YAML in Console and API: name, metrics, algorithm, safety limits, cooldowns, and labels. Console pages show weighted metric score and simulation view (what-if scale decisions for last 60m).

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Threshold is simple and predictable vs. PID/predictive which require tuning and can overshoot. We'll provide sane defaults and auto-tuning helpers (baseline Kp/Ki from historical load).
- Predictive scaler reduces SLO violations for bursty traffic but increases risk of overprovisioning; tie predictive aggressiveness to committed capacity tier (higher tiers can use more aggressive prediction).
- Weighted metric approach lets customers prefer throughput vs. latency; but increases complexity — provide templates for common workloads.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Policy model + API + UI scaffolding (2 sprints): implement storage, validation, and basic threshold algorithm + safety limits enforcement.
2) PID controller integration + auto-tune helper (2 sprints): test across synthetic and replayed workloads.
3) Predictive scaler + simulation & chaos testing (3 sprints): run canaries on low-risk fleets and measure customer impact.
4) Fleet-level optimizer and cost-aware routing (post-MVP): global decisions to move load vs. scale.

Telemetry & observability requirements:
- Expose per-policy metrics: weighted_violation_score, decision_reason, proposed_delta, executed_delta, cooldown_remaining.
- Track suppressed actions due to safety limits and record event history for audits.
- Integrate with Console rollout view and Alerts (SLO breach risk > 10% triggers).

Acceptance criteria:
- Customers can create/modify autoscaling policies via API/Console.
- Policies enforce min/max capacity and scale rate limits under load tests.
- PID and predictive algorithms demonstrably reduce p95 violations compared to baseline (A/B test on canary fleets).
- Observability surfaces decision rationale and safety-limit hits in Console.

Links and artifacts:
- Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/autoscale-policy-engine (draft)
comments: 2025-11-12 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket to centralize autoscaling policy work for Dedicated. Initial sketch attached to Confluence. Asked infra team for capacity model data.

2025-11-13 - Connor Liu: Ran offline experiments replaying 72h of customer traffic. Baseline threshold scaler shows repeated p95 spikes during short ramps. PID reduced spike duration but overshot by ~8% in 2 tests.
2025-11-14 - Marta Gómez (PM): Prioritize latency-first templates for enterprise customers and cost-first templates for startups. Agreed to expose templates in Console. Added to project backlog.

2025-11-16 - Security Review (notes): No new data plane surface; policy metadata is control-plane only. Marked security_review_required=false pending final review on predictive model telemetry retention.

2025-11-18 - Engineering: Implemented API schema v1 and basic threshold scaler. Integration tests for min/max capacity and rate limits added. See PR #1289. Requesting design review for PID parameters UI.

2025-11-20 - Connor Liu: Spike results for predictive scaler finished. Predictive (EWMA+trend) reduced expected p95 SLA breach window by ~35% at the cost of ~6% extra node-hours when tuned aggressively. Propose conservative default and cluster-level opt-in.
2025-11-20 - Next steps: Finish PID auto-tune helper, add simulation mode in Console, and schedule canary rollout for selected internal fleets week of 2025-11-30.
